problem: It takes $35$ seconds for a dolphin to swim $315$ meters at a constant pace. How long does it take for the dolphin to swim $396$ meters?

feedback.problem: It takes $4$ hours for a marathon runner to run $20$ miles at a constant pace. How long does it take for the marathon runner to run $26$ miles?
feedback.worked_solution:
Speed is a special unit rate applied to moving objects. It is defined as *the distance traveled per unit of time*:

$$
\text{speed}=\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}
$$

To find the speed, in miles per hour, we divide the number of miles, which is $20,$ by the number of hours, $4.$ This gives,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{20}{4} & =20÷4 \\  & =5.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the speed of the marathon runner is $5$ miles per hour. 

To find the time it takes the marathon runner to cover $26$ miles, we divide the distance by $5.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{time} & =\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{speed}} \\  & =\frac{26}{5} \\  & =26÷5 \\  & =5.2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, it takes the marathon runner $5.2$ hours to run $26$ miles.
